newsitem.title: UK: UK stocks end higher as Dow firms, trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: UK stocks end higher as Dow firms, trade quiet.

text.p: UK shares ended modestly higher on Monday, underpinned by a firmer Wall Street, but trading volumes were thin as investors remained wary about a possible near-term Dow sell-off, dealers said.
"At the end of the day we still have quite a bit of uncertainty. People are reluctant to buy at what could be the top of the market," one dealer said.
The FTSE 100 ended 21.4 points higher at 3,993.8.
"To say it has been dull is an understatement. It has been like watching paint dry today, except without the excitement," the head of trading at a large stockbrokers said.
The top 100 index traded in a narrow 17-point trading range, while volume was a meagre 495 million shares by 1630 GMT.

A solid start on Wall Street was one of a the few bright spots in an otherwise dull London market. The Dow industrials soared 50 points in the opening minutes, lifted by news of the $13 billion merger between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas.
The Dow was up 31 points at 6,336 by the London close.
The low trading volumes continued to underscore the market's general nervousness over a possible near-term slide on Wall Street, dealers said.
The Dow, which fell a net 77 points last week is still sporting a 26 percent gain so far this year, despite dropping four percent since reaching an all-time peak of 6,606 on November 26.

"It is not unreasonable to believe U.S. shares will drop again," the head of sales and trading at a major investment bank said. "They've run up more than 50 percent in two years. A 10 percent correction from here would not be out of the ordinary."
Technical analysts believe the FTSE will test lower levels in the near-term before attempting to make any sustained upward move.

"The bias at the moment has to be toward the downside," one analyst said. "On the daily charts, the FTSE is still overbought." The FTSE has some near-term support at the 3,933-44 level, with strong support at 3,885-3,990, the analyst said.
UK gilts ended little changed in an uninspired session. The March long gilt future finished at 109-2/32, up 1/32.

British Sky Broadcasting was one of the most active shares of the session, rising 13p at 489-1/2, after the satellite broadcaster cleared a key regulatory hurdle amid reports it planned to push ahead and launch digital services in Britain next year.
British Telecom gained 3p to 393-1/2 amid positive comment on the stock following Friday's announcement that it was buying a stake in a new Swiss telecoms group.
Elsewhere, profit-taking took the shine off B.A.T Industries, down 11p at 479-1/2, while continued worries about broker downgrades pushed Glaxo Wellcome 5p lower at 937-1/2.
Gibbs Mew plunged 86-1/2p or 29 percent at 212-1/2, after the brewer reported a drop in first-half pre-tax profits and warned that full-year results would be lower than the same period a year ago.
